title: Margins prompt
text: To figure out the top candidate and the runner up, I turned to ChatGPT. This is the prompt and return.

title: Margins prompt
text:
Prompt
I have the following data in R:

tibble::tribble(
  ~year, ~district, ~name, ~party, ~candvotes,
  "2016", 46, "Dukes", "D", 37457, 
  "2016", 46, "Greeley", "G", 2178,
  "2016", 46, "Ludlow", "L", 3445,
  "2016", 46, "Nila", "R", 10209 ) 


  



And I want new columns that do the following:

the name of the winning candidate (highest candvotes value).
the percentage of the total vote that the winning candidate received
the name of the second highest candidate (using candvotes)
the percentage of the total vote that second candidate got
the difference betwen the two percentages

title: Margins prompt
text:
The result
You can do this cleanly with dplyr by working within each year–district, ranking candidates by votes, and then summarizing.
Here’s a tidyverse solution that gives one row per race with all the fields you want.
library(dplyr)

df <- tibble::tribble(
  ~year, ~district,     ~name, ~party, ~candvotes,
  "2016",        46,   "Dukes",    "D",      37457,
  "2016",        46, "Greeley",    "G",       2178,
  "2016",        46,  "Ludlow",    "L",       3445,
  "2016",        46,    "Nila",    "R",      10209
)

result <- df %>%
  group_by(year, district) %>%
  mutate(
    total_votes = sum(candvotes),
    pct = candvotes / total_votes * 100
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(candvotes), .by_group = TRUE) %>%
  summarise(
    winner = first(name),
    winner_pct = first(pct),
    runner_up = nth(name, 2),
    runner_up_pct = nth(pct, 2),
    pct_diff = winner_pct - runner_up_pct,
    .groups = "drop"
  )

result

Output
# A tibble: 1 × 7
  year  district winner winner_pct runner_up runner_up_pct pct_diff
  <chr>    <dbl> <chr>       <dbl> <chr>            <dbl>    <dbl>
1 2016        46 Dukes        70.2  Nila             19.2     51.0


Why this works

group_by(year, district) → treats each race separately
total_votes → denominator for percentages
arrange(desc(candvotes), .by_group = TRUE) → ensures winners are first
first() and nth(2) → safely grab top two finishers
pct_diff → margin of victory in percentage points



Optional: keep party labels too
If you want winner/runner-up party as well:
summarise(
  winner = first(name),
  winner_party = first(party),
  winner_pct = first(pct),
  runner_up = nth(name, 2),
  runner_up_party = nth(party, 2),
  runner_up_pct = nth(pct, 2),
  pct_diff = winner_pct - runner_up_pct,
  .groups = "drop"
)
If you want this to scale to multi-year, multi-district election data, this pattern will hold without modification.

title: Calculate margins
text:
Updates Dec. 2025
The first attempt at this compared the highest votes received to the lowest votes received. What we needed was the difference between the percentage of total vote of those finishing 1st and 2nd in each race, which this now does. It’s a complete refactoring.

title: Calculate margins
text:
Setup and import


Expand this to see code
library(tidyverse)
library(janitor)

# general <- read_rds("data-processed/01-general-results-rep.rds")
# primary <- read_rds("data-processed/01-primary-results-rep.rds")
reps <- read_rds("data-processed/01-rep-totals.rds")

title: Calculate margins
text:
Calculate win margin
This summarise method was developed with the help of chatGPT. It’s explained here.


Expand this to see code
reps_calcs <- reps |> 
  group_by(year, election, district) |>
  mutate(
    total_votes = sum(candvotes),
    pct = (candvotes / total_votes * 100) |> round(2)
  ) |>
  arrange(desc(candvotes), .by_group = TRUE)  |> 
  summarise(
    winner = first(name),
    winner_party = first(party),
    winner_inc = first(incumbent),
    winner_pct = first(pct),
    runner_up = nth(name, 2),
    runner_up_party = nth(party, 2),
    runner_up_inc = nth(incumbent, 2),
    runner_up_pct = nth(pct, 2),
    winning_margin = (winner_pct - runner_up_pct) |> round_half_up(2),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |> 
  arrange(year, election, district)

reps_calcs |> head()



  




Add flags
Here we add flags if the race is competitive within 5 or 10 points.
Just showing the margin and flags to check.


Expand this to see code
reps_flags <- reps_calcs |> 
  mutate(flg_5 = if_else(winning_margin <= 5, T, F),
         flg_10 = if_else(winning_margin <= 10, T, F))

# peek at flags
reps_flags |>
  head(20) |> 
  select(winning_margin:flg_10)

title: Overview
text:
The purpose of this project is to find which Texas House of Representatives races have been competitive in past years.
We start with election results by Voting Tabulation Districts as provided by the Texas Legislative Council: Comprehensive Election Datasets (Compressed Format) | Docs.
From that data we calculate statewide results, find the two candidates in each district that have the most votes, and then calculate a margin of victory.
The processing of these results yields two files, an 02-reps-margins.rds version that end up in data-processed folder, and a 02-reps-margins.csv version end up in the data-export folder.
